relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.role: Sir Thomas Adams's Professor of Arabic
relations.evidence: Edward Granville Browne (7 February 1862 – 5 January 1926) was a British Iranologist and Sir Thomas Adams's Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge.

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Browne attended Newcastle College of Physical Science from 1877 to 1879.

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Browne enrolled at Pembroke College, Cambridge... After graduating with a BA in 1882

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Whilst at Cambridge, Browne studied Arabic under Edward Henry Palmer and William Wright

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Returning to the University of Cambridge, Browne studied for an Indian languages tripos Master's (comprising Hindustani, Sanskrit, Persian, and Arabic) from 1882 to 1884.

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Resuming his medical studies at St Bartholomew's Hospital, Browne graduated with a Bachelor of Medicine in 1887.

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Made a Fellow of Pembroke College in 1887

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: In 1888, whilst still travelling, Browne was appointed a university lecturer in Persian at University of Cambridge.

relations.subject: Edward Granville Browne
relations.evidence: Browne met Haji Pirzadeh Naeini, a famous intellectual-mystic and world traveler of the Qajar era, through whom he broadened his interest and knowledge of Persian history, culture, and language.
